findings.description: Long-lived AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in cleartext in the Lambda function's environment variables and committed to source control. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration or read access to the repository obtains usable AWS credentials.

No kms_key_arn is configured, so the environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are visible in plaintext to any principal that can describe the function. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy is required to control access to these values.
The function uses nodejs12.x, which has reached end of support and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving known vulnerabilities in the runtime unaddressed.

No vpc_config block is defined, so the function runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary, easing data exfiltration if the function or its dependencies are compromised.
